seal.statement: The owner's rule (2026-09-18): the whole corpus is never run on GitHub-hosted runners when a local alternative exists, releases included. Until now every push whose gate proved only a cone owed a 74-minute corpus run on a hosted runner in the full-corpus canary. The canary now moves local. After a verified push whose gate proved a cone, the publisher starts, detached, a run of exactly the rest of the corpus for the pushed commit - the files the cone did not already prove at that commit, so nothing it just proved runs again - in a fresh exact checkout, where placement spreads it over the lab machines. Green, it records the whole-corpus receipt for that commit; red, the next publish says so before anything else. A newer publish supersedes a running one, as the hosted canary's cancel-in-progress did, because only the newest head matters. The hosted canary runs only when dispatched by hand, and a release proves its exact commit locally and records release-full-v1, so full-gate reuses it rather than waking a remote runner.

text: The local corpus lives in scripts/publish-head.js (no new script). The gate's proof scope now lists the files a cone proved (select-change-tests writeProofScope testPaths). After a verified push, when that scope names a cone for the pushed commit, the publisher computes the rest of the corpus - what test:all runs (its filter read from package.json and planned by plan-test-lane) minus the cone - writes it to <git-common-dir>/lagrange-local-corpus/<sha>.files and starts `publish-head.js --local-corpus <sha>` detached in its own group with the gate's retry policy. That mode runs push-gate-corpus-worktree --gate <sha> --run (the classified runner on the list, so placement spreads it over the lab), and only when it exits 0 records corpus-full-v1 for the commit; a red run records red, a record failure is named on a green one, and a run superseded meanwhile keeps the newer publish's word. Every publish first reports: every red since the last green, loudest, then the newest record; then it supersedes any running local corpus (SIGTERM to its group, only when /proc shows it is one) and names a dead one lost; keeps the newest 20 records. None of it can fail a publish. full-corpus-canary.yml loses its automatic trigger (hand dispatch only); RELEASE.md step 4 proves the release locally (push-gate-corpus-worktree --gate <sha> --run npm run check:release, then record release-full-v1), full-gate/GCP only as the fallback; the pre-push header and the solver runbook say the same. Seven tests in test/scripts/local-corpus.test.js, including an end-to-end publish in the publisher's own fixture shape (red reported first, the rest started for the pushed commit without the cone's file).

round 1 REJECT (4 blocking). B1: the publisher superseded any running local corpus at the start of a publish, before its own gate; a gate that then failed or was interrupted left the proof of the commit still on origin/main stopped, marked superseded by a commit never pushed, and nothing restarted it (reproduced). B2: the report was written before the supersede step decided the state, so a lost or superseded run printed as running and the newer publish's record was always the one shown - red-is-reported broken (reproduced). B3: nothing tested the scope writer: writeProofScope writing testPaths null kept all 7 local-corpus tests and 126 related assertions green, while in real use every publish would print "not started" (the canary-proof-reuse failure shape). B4: RELEASE.md step 4 gave prove and record as two lines; pasted together, record release-full-v1 runs even when the proof fails and the tag workflow publishes on that receipt. Non-blocking: N1 no thermal wait before the detached run; N2 convergence probes no longer ran anywhere automatically; N3 the detached run lived in the publishing checkout (usually a quest worktree), whose removal after landing would read as RED; N4 unreadable /proc (macOS) assumed a local corpus and signalled; N5 no error listener on the detached child, a spawn failure would exit a finished publish 1. Held: cone plus rest is exactly the whole corpus, no stale or foreign scope leaks, a whole-corpus gate starts nothing, CI's scope reader ignores the new field; end to end in a throwaway clone with a temporary remote - supersede stopped the whole group and removed the exact checkout, a green run recorded corpus-full-v1 through the hook's fast path, a red run recorded nothing and the next report led with RED; all requested checks plus file-size, duplication, unused exports, circular dependencies green; harness 6/6; 10 of 11 mutations killed (the survivor is B3).

round 1 repair. B1: supersede moved after the verified push (localCorpusAfterPush), so a failed or interrupted publish touches nothing; and a running record for the very head being published is never its own successor (sha !== head guard, witnessed). B2: every publish first reconciles (a running record whose process is gone becomes lost, no signals), then reports; red and lost both get a banner since the last green, superseded is named with "a newer head on main", and supersedeLocalCorpus writes its own line when it stops one. B3: the cone-publish receipt now drives the real writer - runDecision plus writeProofScope into a temp scope root - so testPaths null fails it (mutation killed). B4: RELEASE.md chains `push-gate-corpus-worktree --gate <sha> --run npm run check:release && proof-authority record release-full-v1 <sha>` and says why. N1: the run waits for thermal headroom first (lost with the reason when the machine stays too hot). N2: the run script observes npm run test:convergence-probes after the corpus, never letting it decide. N3: the detached run starts from the main checkout (dirname of the common git dir) and keeps its state in <common>/lagrange-local-corpus, so quest-worktree removal cannot touch it. N4: fail-closed identity - no /proc and no ps answer means not ours, never signalled. N5: error listener on the child marks the record lost; bookkeeping never fails a publish. Statement updated to match (supersede only after a verified push; thermal wait; convergence probes observed; release record only when green). Repair mutations 9/9 killed plus the same-head guard witness. Pre-commit, complexity 1819/1819 and cognitive 160/160, audit:shards, unused:push, publish-head, workspace-links, select-change-tests, push-gate-change-proof, canary-corpus-needed green; harness 6/6.

round 2 REJECT (2 blocking). B1-B4, N1, N2, N5 confirmed repaired by mutation and real runs (9 of 11 round-2 mutations killed). B5 (new): the same-head guard in supersedeLocalCorpus kept the running proof alive, but localCorpusAfterPush then started a second run for the same sha, rewriting .files, truncating the shared log and replacing the record's pid - two heavy runs at once, the first untracked (a newer head supersedes only the second), and if the first finishes green the second takes the non-running record for superseded and drops its own red; reproduced (same-head.mjs, red-dropped.mjs) by re-running npm run publish on a head already on origin/main. B6 (process): the sealed statement in quest.json was edited in place; R09 - a sealed contract is superseded, never reinterpreted - and solve only checks doneWhen, so land would not catch it; the round-2 code already satisfies the sealed text. Non-blocking: N3 and N4 repairs untested (mainRoot: root and a fail-open identity check both survive); the detached run's wrapper scripts (thermal, materializer, proof-authority, pre-push) come from the main checkout on disk, which can lag origin/main; convergence probes add about 3 minutes after every publish, even when red, and their result lives only in the pruned log; release step 4 has no thermal wait and nothing coordinates it with a running local corpus; round-1 N7/N8 stand (a publish with LAGRANGE_PUSH_SKIP_TESTS starts nothing, PR merges get no corpus, focused-contract files rerun in the rest). Real end to end in a throwaway clone: a green run started from the main checkout survived removal of the quest worktree mid-run and recorded corpus-full-v1 through the hook's fast path; a supersede stopped the whole group including the sh wrapper, the probes never started, the exact checkout was removed. All checks green, harness 6/6, probe done.

round 2 repair. B5: localCorpusAfterPush, after supersede (which reconciles first), looks for a record of the very head being published that still counts - running (alive, since reconcile just ran) or green - and then starts nothing, saying "publish: local corpus not started: already running|green for this commit"; a lost, red or superseded one is run again. Witness 'publishing the same head again starts no second run beside the first' publishes one head twice through the real publisher (the second push a no-op) with a live fake run: one spawn, the record still running; green covers it too; lost starts again. Mutations killed: guard off, green not covering, lost covering. B6: quest.json statement restored byte for byte from the seal record; the clarifications stay in the round-1 repair attempt. N3 witness 'the local corpus runs from the main checkout, not the worktree that published' publishes from a linked quest worktree and requires the spawn's cwd to be the main checkout (mainRoot: root mutation killed). N4 witness 'a process whose command line cannot be read is never taken for a local corpus' uses a real zombie (answers kill 0, empty /proc cmdline): reconcile names its record lost (fail-open mutation killed). Release step 4 now starts with wait-for-thermal-headroom and says to let a running local corpus finish first. Not changed, recorded: wrapper scripts from the main checkout (compatible today; the tests themselves run from the pushed sha); probes after a red corpus (observed as the hosted canary did); N7/N8. Pre-commit, ratchets 1819/1819 and 160/160, audit:shards, unused:push, publish-head, select-change-tests, local-corpus (10 tests) green; harness 6/6.

round 3 APPROVE (no blocking). B5 fixed: localCorpusAfterPush supersedes (reconciling first), then starts nothing when the head already has a live running or a green record, saying "not started: already <state> for this commit"; the round-2 reproduction same-head.mjs through the real publisher now starts 1 run, not 2, and the record keeps the live pid; mutations killed (guard off, green not covering, lost covering); a red or lost same-head record runs again, acceptable since the red was reported first. B6 fixed: statement and doneWhen match the seal record exactly; the log only grew. N3 and N4 now witnessed (mainRoot: root and fail-open mutations killed); local-corpus.test.js 12/12 runs green with no fake or zombie process left. RELEASE.md step 4 chains thermal wait, exact-checkout proof and record with &&, and says to let a running local corpus finish first. B1, B2, B3 mutations re-checked, still killed. Non-blocking: red same-head rerun untested (adding red to the covering set survives); an earlier red keeps its banner until a later local corpus is green even when a gate proved the whole corpus (too loud, never silent); wrapper scripts from the main checkout, probes after a red corpus, round-1 N7/N8 recorded. Checks green (static and unit only): eslint, literals, decision boundaries, complexity 1819/1819, cognitive 160/160, audit:shards, unused:push, file-size, unused exports 1438/1438, circular 0/0, duplication 57/57 and 793/793, six unit test files 129 assertions, harness 6/6, probe done.
